newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares close lower on industrial data.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares close lower on industrial data.

text.p: Chilean stocks drifted lower in light afternoon trading on Monday as fresh data issued by a private business organization pointed to sluggish economic growth, brokers said.
The blue-chip IPSA closed 0.10 percent lower at 119.22 points. The all-share IGPA dipped 0.05 percent to end at 5354.44 points on slow volume of 100 million shares traded.
Investors paid little heed to gains on Wall Street and noted figures from the influential private trade group Sofofa showing an unexpected 3.6 percent drop in industrial output in March.
Most of the big electricals closed lower, including Endesa, which fell 0.9 percent to 257 pesos and Chilgener, off 0.4 percent to 169.5 pesos.

Banco Santiago shares fell after the company announced plans for a $150 million capital increase and that it would place its E series, now held by the Central Bank, on the bourse. The bank's C series fell 2.7 percent to 9.9 pesos.

One of the few bright spots was in the paper sector, where epxectations of strong pulp prices drove up prices, brokers said. Copec was up 1.5 percent to 1655 pesos, and its archcompetitor CMPC was up 0.4 percent to 4420 pesos.
"Figures like this affect the market in general, but the problem is that the market is already soft," said one broker.
The Sofofa figures hit the market while it was rising weakly amid light turnover, backtracking in the afternoon session.

The government will issue April inflation, quarterly unemployment and its own industrial production figures early Tuesday. The figures are "90 percent factored into the market," as one broker put it, but eyes were already looking toward the March and first-quarter growth figures to be issued by the Central Bank on May 23.
Foodmaker Iansa was on the rebound after it fell last week on disappointing first-quarter earnings, ending 2.8 percent higher at 74 pesos.
Brokers saw prospects for a technical rebound on Tuesday, but said the bourse remained basically without direction and volatile.
"We're dealing with a slow market that has no real tendency behind it," said one.
